questions.section: PART TWO Structured Question (10 X 6=60 marks)
questions.question:
1. Atoms of Carbon are shown below

   | A   | B   | C   |
   | ¹²C | ¹³C | ¹⁴C |

  a. State the number of protons in atom A and B. (2 Marks)
  b. State the number of neutrons in atom A and B. (2 Marks)
  c. What do mean by the term Isotope? (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. A = 6 protons; B = 6 protons (all carbon atoms have atomic number 6).
b. A: 12 − 6 = 6 neutrons; B: 13 − 6 = 7 neutrons.
c. Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons (atomic number) but different numbers of neutrons (different mass numbers).

questions.section: PART TWO Structured Question (10 X 6=60 marks)
questions.question:
2. The table below shows two Ions:

   | A           | B          |
   | ⁴⁰₂₀Ca²⁺    | ³⁵₁₇Cl⁻    |

  a. State the number of electrons of the above ions. (2 Marks)
  b. Write the electronic configuration (in Spdf) of particle A? (2 Marks)
  c. Write down the electronic arrangement (in Spdf) of particle B?(2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Ca²⁺: 20 − 2 = 18 electrons; Cl⁻: 17 + 1 = 18 electrons.
b. Ca²⁺: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶
c. Cl⁻: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ (both ions are isoelectronic with argon).

questions.section: PART TWO Structured Question (10 X 6=60 marks)
questions.question:
6. Define the following terms:-
  a. i) Exothermic process. (1 Marks)
     ii) Endothermic process. (1 Marks)
  b. Bond energy. (2 Marks)
  c. Enthalpy change. (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. i) A process (reaction) that releases heat energy to the surroundings; ΔH is negative.
   ii) A process that absorbs heat energy from the surroundings; ΔH is positive.
b. Bond energy is the energy needed to break one mole of a particular covalent bond (in gaseous molecules); the same amount is released when the bond forms.
c. Enthalpy change (ΔH) is the heat energy given out or taken in during a chemical reaction at constant pressure (ΔH = H products − H reactants).

questions.section: PART TWO Structured Question (10 X 6=60 marks)
questions.question:
8. The table below show PH of some acids Alkalis.

   | A  | B | C | D | E |
   | 14 | 1 | 6 | 8 | 7 |

   Which of the above substance is a:-
  a. i) Weak acid (1 Mark)
     ii) Weak alkali (1 Mark)
  b. i) Strong acid (1 Mark)
     ii) Strong Alkali (1 Mark)
  c. Name one weak acid and one weak alkali in everyday life. (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. i) C (pH 6)
   ii) D (pH 8)
b. i) B (pH 1)
   ii) A (pH 14)
   (E, pH 7, is neutral.)
c. Weak acid (any one): vinegar (ethanoic acid), lemon juice (citric acid), carbonic acid in soda drinks. Weak alkali (any one): ammonia solution, baking soda (sodium hydrogencarbonate), toothpaste, soap solution.

  a. What is Air pollution? (2 Marks)
  b. State two source of Air pollution? (2 Marks)
  c. List any two Pollutant gases. (2 Marks)

questions.answer_guide:
a. Air pollution is the presence in the air of harmful substances (gases, smoke, dust) in amounts that damage living things, materials or the environment.
b. Any two: burning fossil fuels in factories and power stations; vehicle exhausts; burning of rubbish/charcoal; forest fires; volcanoes; dust from mining and construction.
c. Any two: carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO₂), nitrogen oxides (NO₂), carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane, CFCs.

questions.answer_guide:
a. The filtrate is the liquid (here, water) that passes through the filter paper and collects in the flask.
b. The residue is the insoluble solid (here, sand) that stays on the filter paper.
c. Filtration.
